description: MPoint (MPM) Python SDK documentation index. Material points are exposed under itasca.mpoint (MPMPoint objects, the mpmpointarray vectorized interface) and background-grid nodes under itasca.mpoint.node (MeshPoint objects, meshpointarray); the FISH mpoint.* intrinsics remain an alternative. The shared continuum modules (itasca.zone, itasca.gridpoint, ...) also run on the MPoint binary but belong to FLAC and are documented under software='flac'.

fallback_hints.model solve: For solving to equilibrium, use itasca.command('model solve'). Python SDK has itasca.cycle() for fixed cycles only.
fallback_hints.automatic timestep: For automatic timestep calculation, use itasca.command('model auto dt'). Python SDK itasca.set_timestep() sets manual values only.
fallback_hints.material point: After 'mpoint import from-zones' the points are itasca.mpoint objects: itasca.mpoint.count(), itasca.mpoint.list(), itasca.mpoint.mpmpointarray.pos()/stress()/velocity(); background-grid nodes are itasca.mpoint.node.list() / itasca.mpoint.node.meshpointarray.pos(). FISH mpoint.* intrinsics (mpoint.list, mpoint.pos, mpoint.node.num) still work for FISH-side scripts.
fallback_hints.mpoint: Material points are itasca.mpoint objects from 9.8: itasca.mpoint.list()/find()/near()/containing() return MPMPoint (pos, velocity, disp, stress, strain, mass, vol, pp, group, extra); itasca.mpoint.mpmpointarray gives the same as numpy arrays. Commands still go through itasca.command('mpoint ...'); FISH mpoint.* intrinsics remain available.
fallback_hints.background node: Background-grid nodes are not itasca.gridpoint objects (that is FLAC's zone-gridpoint API, and the gridpoints go away at 'mpoint import'). They are itasca.mpoint.node: list()/find()/near() return MeshPoint (pos, velocity, force_unbal, radius, grav_mass), itasca.mpoint.node.meshpointarray gives arrays, and node.stress(point)/pp(point)/disp(point) sample the grid at a position. FISH mpoint.node.* intrinsics remain available.
fallback_hints.grid node: Background-grid nodes are not itasca.gridpoint objects (that is FLAC's zone-gridpoint API, and the gridpoints go away at 'mpoint import'). They are itasca.mpoint.node: list()/find()/near() return MeshPoint (pos, velocity, force_unbal, radius, grav_mass), itasca.mpoint.node.meshpointarray gives arrays, and node.stress(point)/pp(point)/disp(point) sample the grid at a position. FISH mpoint.node.* intrinsics remain available.
fallback_hints.from-zones: 'mpoint import from-zones' deletes the zones and their gridpoints, so itasca.zone.count() and itasca.gridpoint.count() both drop to 0 afterwards. Read zone state before converting.
fallback_hints.itasca.zone: itasca.zone and itasca.gridpoint run on the MPoint binary -- all 236 documented functions are present -- but they are FLAC's continuum API and are documented under software='flac'. Note they only see the pre-conversion grid: 'mpoint import' deletes the zones.
fallback_hints.itasca.gridpoint: itasca.gridpoint is FLAC's zone-gridpoint API, documented under software='flac'. It is NOT the MPM background grid -- that is itasca.mpoint.node (MeshPoint objects, meshpointarray).

live_verification_mpoint3d_98: itasca.mpoint verified on live MPoint3D 9.8.54 (2026-10-28): after a 512-point 'mpoint import from-zones' (node spacing 0.5, 729 mesh points), itasca.mpoint.count() returned 512, mpmpointarray.pos() shape (512, 3), stress() shape (512, 3, 3), node.stress((1,1,1)) a stens3. Cycling needs 'model large-strain on' first.
